title: Spiced Gingerbread Latte Cupcakes
shortDescription: Warm gingerbread cupcakes with espresso buttercream, ready in about 25 minutes prep and 18 minutes bake.
description: These cupcakes taste like a gingerbread latte in cake form. I tested this batch three times before the spice mix felt right for a home oven.
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F. Line a 12-cup muffin pan with paper liners.
Whisk flour, baking soda, baking powder, ginger, cinnamon, cloves, nutmeg, and salt in a bowl.
In a large bowl, beat 1/2 cup butter and brown sugar until fluffy, about 2 minutes.
Add molasses and eggs to the butter mix. Beat until smooth and well combined.
Mix in buttermilk and 1 tbsp espresso. Add dry ingredients in two batches, mixing just until combined.
Divide batter evenly among liners, filling each about two-thirds full.
Bake 16 to 18 minutes, until a toothpick comes out clean. Cool in pan 5 minutes, then move to a wire rack.
For frosting, beat 1 cup butter until pale and creamy, about 3 minutes.
Add powdered sugar in two batches, then mix in 2 tbsp espresso and vanilla until smooth and fluffy.
Cool cupcakes completely, then pipe frosting high. Dust with cinnamon before serving.
tips: Room temperature eggs and buttermilk blend faster and give a smoother batter.
Use fresh ground spices if you can. Old spice jars lose punch fast.
Let espresso cool fully before adding it to frosting, or it will melt the butter.
These cupcakes taste even better the next day, once the spices settle in.

faq.question: Can I use instant coffee instead of brewed espresso?
faq.answer: Yes. Dissolve 1 tsp instant espresso powder in 1 tbsp hot water for the batter, and 2 tsp in 2 tbsp hot water for the frosting.

faq.question: Why did my gingerbread cupcakes sink in the middle?
faq.answer: This usually means the oven door was opened too early, or the baking soda was old. Check freshness and avoid opening the oven before minute 14.

faq.question: Can I make these cupcakes ahead for a holiday party?
faq.answer: Bake the cupcakes up to 2 days ahead and store unfrosted at room temperature in an airtight container. Frost the morning of your event for best texture.

faq.question: Is the frosting very sweet with all that sugar?
faq.answer: The espresso cuts through the sweetness so it does not taste like plain sugar frosting. If you prefer less sweet, reduce powdered sugar to 2 1/2 cups.

conclusion: These cupcakes bring gingerbread and coffee shop flavor into one holiday bake. Serve them warm from frosting for your next winter gathering, and share with friends who love a spiced latte.
